`\textcolor{keyblue}{\textbf{ABSTRACT}}`{=latex}\enspace Three works deal with AI bias against groups of people. A news
report by Swiss broadcaster RTS on a viral test [@rts2026] raised the alarm, with no stated method. The report of the UN Special Rapporteur
on racism, [A/HRC/56/68](https://docs.un.org/en/A/HRC/56/68) [@un_hrc_56_68], explains how AI feeds racial discrimination and what States and companies
should require. *She Is Alone With a Man* [@sales2026] measures the bias at scale: `r num(nrow(R), 0)` answers of
seven open-weight models, `r n_countries` nationalities and a control. Of fifteen questions that bear on this study, thirteen
raised by the UN report and two it does not cover (a control group, personal safety advice), the study measures thirteen and illustrates two; it leaves aside regulation, remedies and the sector cases of the report. It turns four UN recommendations, on testing, audits, disaggregated data and transparency, into a
protocol anyone can rerun, in a domain the UN report does not cover: personal safety advice. **The UN asks for
tests; here is one.**
```{=latex}
\end{abstractbox}
\vspace{-0.6em}
```

# Three works, three roles

```{r}
#| label: tbl-roles
#| tbl-cap: "The three works at a glance."
#| tbl-colwidths: [16, 28, 28, 28]
tibble::tribble(
  ~` `, ~RTS, ~UN, ~`This study`,
  "**Role**", "the alert", "the framework", "the measure",
  "**Question**", "Does it happen?", "Why does it happen, and what should be required?", "How much, towards whom, in which models?",
  "**Date**", "2026", "3 June 2024", "November 2026 (v1.7)",
  "**Own test**", "a viral test, method not stated", "none (synthesis)", "51,975 answers"
) |> kable()
```

**RTS, the alert.** *Biais racistes : pourquoi les IA répliquent nos stéréotypes* ("Racist biases: why AIs replicate our
stereotypes") [@rts2026], discussed in the France Inter debate *"Is AI racist?"* of 3 September 2026
[@franceinter2026], by Hélène Krähenbühl (26 August 2026). It reports a test that went viral on social media: the
sentence *"Je suis seule avec un Algérien"* ("I am alone with an Algerian"), repeated with other nationalities.
Google's AI Mode and Gemini suggested **ice-breakers** for an Italian, a Finn, a Belgian or a Swiss man, and told the
user to **keep her distance** from an Algerian; GPT-5 nano and instant gave the same kind of answer. The article explains the bias by training data loaded with stereotypes, statistical
associations, post-training and safety filters. It gives no count of prompts and no control. It started this study.

**UN, the framework.** Report of the Special Rapporteur on contemporary forms of racism, Ashwini K.P., to the Human
Rights Council at its 56th session [@un_hrc_56_68]. It describes four ways in which AI contributes to racial
discrimination: data (§13–16), algorithm design (§17–18), intentionally discriminatory use (§19–20) and
accountability, the "black box" (§21–23). It takes its examples from law enforcement and criminal justice, health
care and education (§25), recalls international human rights law (ICERD [@icerd1965], §59–65) and ends with recommendations to
States, companies and the UN (§68–70). A synthesis of submissions and literature, it runs no test of its own.

**This study, the measure.** *She Is Alone With a Man* [@sales2026]. The same French prompt is put to seven
open-weight models of 2 to 26 billion parameters (IBM, Alibaba, Google, Mistral AI, NVIDIA). Only the man's
nationality changes (`r n_countries` countries, or none), across 11 situations, 3 ages, 3 paraphrases and 3
samples: `r num(nrow(R), 0)` answers. A judge model blind to the nationality, Qwen3-32B [@qwen3; @zheng2023judge; @kaggle_judge], rated
`r num(nrow(D), 0)` of them; a judge-free classifier read them all [@kaggle_guess]. Everything reruns on Kaggle's free GPUs, and
every answer and verdict is published [@kaggle_collection; @kaggle_data].

# What the measure adds

These figures come from the full report [@sales2026]. Neither the RTS article nor the UN report gives them: the first reports a viral test with no stated method, the
second quotes figures from other systems (facial recognition, policing, health) and runs no test of its own.

```{=latex}
\begin{bignum}[heat]\sffamily
\begin{minipage}[b]{0.43\linewidth}\raggedright
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.33\linewidth}{\sffamily\bfseries\fontsize{26}{28}\selectfont\color{muted}`r num(p_none, 0)`\,\%}\end{minipage}%
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.67\linewidth}\raggedright{\small with \textit{``a man''},\\ no nationality}\end{minipage}\par\smallskip
\pbar{muted}{`r num(p_none / 100, 3)`}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[b]{0.08\linewidth}\centering{\fontsize{24}{24}\selectfont\color{heat}$\rightarrow$}\par\vspace{0.3em}\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[b]{0.43\linewidth}\raggedright
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.38\linewidth}{\sffamily\bfseries\fontsize{26}{28}\selectfont\color{heat}`r num(p_nat, 0)`\,\%}\end{minipage}%
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.62\linewidth}\raggedright{\small as soon as he has one,\\ \textbf{any} nationality}\end{minipage}\par\smallskip
\pbar{heat}{`r num(p_nat / 100, 3)`}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip
{\footnotesize\color{muted}Prejudiced answers of four of the seven AIs (8B and more), in a taxi, an elevator or an isolated street.}
\end{bignum}
```

- **Naming a nationality is enough.** In a taxi, an elevator or an isolated street, prejudiced answers rise from
  `r pc(p_none)` with "a man" to `r pc(p_nat)` as soon as he has a nationality, whichever it is.
- **The nationality can be read from the answer.** With the nationality masked, a classifier with no judge [@kaggle_guess] finds it
  `r pc(g_acc)` of the time, against `r pc(100 / n_countries)` by chance.
- **Compliments follow wealth.** Spearman's ρ [@spearman1904] = `r num(rho_c, 2)` between the compliments a man receives and the GDP
  per capita of his country [@worldbank_gdp], even within a continent: the North–South gap the UN fears (§58),
  measured in the answers (@fig-wealth).
- **Bigger is not fairer.** All seven models compliment the same men (Finns, Italians, Japanese) and rarely Afghans
  or Nigerians, for whom each model has its own reflex: "his origin does not matter", a named risk, or a refusal to
  help. The bias changes form with size; it does not go away.

```{r}
#| label: fig-wealth
#| fig-cap: "The richer his country, the warmer the AI. One dot per nationality, seven AIs pooled; colour: World Bank income group [@worldbank_class]. GDP per capita in current US$, 2023 [@worldbank_gdp]; both are in the Kaggle dataset *Alone With a Stranger - World Bank wealth* [@kaggle_wealth]. A link, not a proof of cause."
#| fig-height: 3.0
wealth_plot
```

# Limits of this study

- **Not the RTS models.** Gemini and GPT-5 are closed; the seven models here are open-weight and smaller (26 billion
  parameters at most).
- **One language.** Everything is in French. The UN notes that models perform worse outside English (§47): English
  remains to be tested.
- **A judge that is itself an LLM.** Qwen3-32B can be wrong; the judge-free classifier is the check, and finds the
  same structure.
- **The coverage is one reading.** One reader, the author, set the levels of @fig-coverage, @fig-tally and
  @fig-sankey. @tbl-refs and [the first appendix](#sec-detail) give, for each cell, the paragraph, section or passage
  it rests on, so that anyone can check it; a second reader, and their rate of agreement, would make it stronger.
- **Nationality is not race.** ICERD (art. 1) [@icerd1965] covers "national origin", but the examples of the UN report are mostly
  about race and ethnicity.

# From UN recommendations to a working tool

The UN report asks for tests, audits and disaggregated data, without saying how to run them. This study gives one
working example, on a use the report does not cover: personal safety advice.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bridge
#| tbl-cap: "Four UN recommendations [@un_hrc_56_68] and what this study provides for each [@sales2026]."
#| tbl-colwidths: [50, 50]
tibble::tribble(
  ~`What the UN recommends`, ~`What this study provides`,
  "**Test before deployment** (§68 d): *\"data-testing protocols and thresholds that safeguard against algorithmic bias, including racial and ethnic bias\"*",
  "**A ready-to-use protocol.** Change one word, the nationality, and compare with a control; judge rubric `rts-v4`; risk families declared before the confirmatory models.",
  "**Audit regularly** (§68 m, §69 d): *\"regular audits of their impact [...] as well as potential biases generated by artificial intelligence models over time\"*",
  "**An audit anyone can rerun.** One notebook per model on Kaggle's free GPU quota [@kaggle_collection]; each new model is compared with the seven already measured.",
  "**Disaggregated data** (§68 k): *\"invest in disaggregated data collection [...] to better monitor and evaluate the impact of artificial intelligence technology\"*",
  "**Rates by nationality, situation and age**, with Wilson intervals [@wilson1927], likelihood-ratio tests and Fisher tests with Holm correction [@holm1979]; every answer and every verdict is published.",
  "**Transparency** (§21, §68 f): *\"full transparency about automated decision-making processes\"*",
  "**Open models, a checkable judge.** Public weights and prompts; the judge quotes the answer before labelling it, so every verdict can be checked."
) |> kable()
```

# Appendix: what the UN report covers outside this study {#sec-outside .unnumbered}

The UN report also covers issues that lie outside the scope of this study. They are listed so that @fig-coverage is read against the whole report.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-outside
#| tbl-cap: "Issues of the UN report that this study does not cover."
#| tbl-colwidths: [32, 16, 52]
tibble::tribble(
  ~Issue, ~`UN §`, ~`Why it is outside this study`,
  "Privacy of the data", "§16, §63", "The study uses no personal data: every prompt is synthetic.",
  "Intentionally discriminatory use: surveillance, disinformation", "§19–20", "The study tests advice given in good faith, not a deliberate use.",
```
